doc.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023

title: Melodic shapes versus hand shapes, sounding like a horn
summary: Bailey thinks of shapes as melodic contours like Parker's lines, trying to sound like a horn player.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: It seems like I’ve seen articles from guitar players and they talk about shapes. Now that can be a hand shape but it also can be what you’re describing as a melodic shape. So which drives which?

Well I tend to think — I mean obviously the guitar is shape oriented. But you know what I always found about — if you, for instance, you take the Charlie Parker “Omni Book” or something — or really any great jazz soloist — and you just squint your eyes you can see the shape of the line. There’s peaks and valleys and that. And that’s what always fascinated me about horn players and why I always try to sound like a horn or [inaudible] because that sense of using the whole range of your instrument. So I think, I think about the shapes more in that way. In intervals, in actual real music than just guitaristically.
